title: Setting for $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$: schemes of finite type over a field
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\neq\ell$. In this
setting all schemes are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are
morphisms of $k$-schemes. No further hypothesis is imposed. For a commutative condensed
ring $\Lambda$ ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]) and a scheme $X$ of the setting, write

$$
D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda):=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda_X)\subseteq D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})
$$

for the bounded constructible derived category ([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]) of
module objects over $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ ([sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]).

Every morphism $f\colon X\to Y$ of the setting has a compactification
$c=(X\xrightarrow{\ i\ }Z\xrightarrow{\ p\ }Y)$ in the sense of [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]:
$f=p\circ i$ with $i$ an open immersion and $p$ proper. The scheme $Z$ is again separated and of
finite type over $k$, and $i$, $p$ are $k$-morphisms, so $c$ stays inside the setting. For every
$f$ we fix one such compactification

$$
c_f=(X\xrightarrow{\ i_f\ }Z_f\xrightarrow{\ p_f\ }Y),
$$

the *chosen compactification* of $f$. It is the compactification used to define $Rf_!$ and
$Rf^!$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$.

proof.text: For the commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$, use [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] to read $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ as a commutative ring object in abelian sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. The category $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ is exactly the module-object category of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Specialize the definition [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] to this ring object and to abelian sheaves: its objects are the bounded complexes with constructible cohomology, and its morphisms are the ambient derived morphisms. The notation $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$ abbreviates this full subcategory. This introduces notation, with no additional condition on $\Lambda$.

source.place: Statement, paragraphs 1–2 and the first display (the coefficient-category notation).

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and write $a_X:X\to S$ and $a_Y:Y\to S$ for the structure morphisms. The affine-scheme lemma [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] makes $S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], finite type of $a_X$ and $a_Y$ includes quasi-compactness. Also $Y$ is quasi-compact as a scheme: apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] to the quasi-compact map $a_Y$ and the quasi-compact base $S$. Thus $X$ is separated and of finite type over $S$, and $Y$ is separated and quasi-compact over $S$, as required in the next step.

source.place: Statement, paragraph 3, compactification-existence assertion; imported proof first sentence, with the quasi-compactness hypotheses made explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-compactification-over-base] with this $S$, these structure morphisms, and the given $S$-morphism $f:X\to Y$. Every hypothesis was checked in step 2, so a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y)$ exists. Unpacking [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], $i$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, $p$ is proper, and $p\circ i=f$. In particular the open-immersion clause in the statement holds with the stronger quasi-compactness included in the referenced definition.

source.place: Statement, paragraph 3, first sentence; imported proof application of lem-sfb-compactification-over-base.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-compactification-middle-over-base] to $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, the structure maps, $f$, and the compactification $c$ of step 3. Step 2 gives the qcqs base; $a_Y$ is separated and of finite type by the setting. The lemma gives $a_Z=a_Y\circ p$ separated and of finite type and makes $i,p$ morphisms over $k$. Thus $Z$ and both maps stay in the setting.

source.place: Statement paragraph 3, closure in the setting; assembly of the extracted middle-scheme lemma (returned steps 4–5).

proof.text: The definition [def-sfb-compactification-over-field] fixes one compactification $c_f$ for precisely these hypotheses on $X$, $Y$ and $f$. Here $Y$ is quasi-compact over $k$ by step 2. Use that already specified choice for the displayed $c_f$; step 4 applies to it as to every compactification. The last sentence of the item records which compactification subsequent shriek constructions use; it does not construct a shriek functor or assert preservation of constructibility or existence of an adjoint for every condensed ring.
